subject: chemistry
title: Ionic compounds: structure and formulae
key_idea: An ionic compound is a giant structure of ions in a regular lattice. Strong electrostatic forces act between oppositely charged ions in all directions. The formula shows the simplest ratio of ions, so that the total charge is zero.

blocks.text: This section describes the structure of an ionic compound such as sodium chloride and how it is represented.

items.meaning: A huge number of particles joined in a repeating pattern.
Strong electrostatic forces of attraction between oppositely charged ions, acting in all directions.

items: Positive and negative ions alternate in a regular pattern.
Each ion is attracted to all the oppositely charged ions around it.
The forces act in all directions through the lattice.
The structure is not made of separate molecules.
A dot and cross diagram shows the electron transfer but not the arrangement of ions in the lattice.
A 2D diagram shows a single layer of ions, not the 3D structure.
A ball and stick model shows the 3D lattice. The sticks suggest bonds between pairs of ions, and the ions are drawn spaced apart.
A diagram of the lattice can be used to show that a compound is ionic: a regular pattern of two types of ion.
An ionic compound is a giant lattice of oppositely charged ions.
Electrostatic forces act in all directions between the ions. This is ionic bonding.
Every model of the lattice has limitations.

blocks.text: The formula of an ionic compound gives the simplest ratio of ions. The charges must add up to zero.

items.text: Count each type of ion in the part of the structure shown.
Write the numbers as a ratio.
Divide by the largest number that goes into both. This is the empirical formula.

rows: Carbonate CO₃²⁻, sulfate SO₄²⁻, phosphate PO₄³⁻

items.text: Two OH⁻ are needed to balance one Ca²⁺.
Ca(OH)₂. Use brackets round a group of atoms when you need more than one.

diagram.alt: Pick a pair of ions to see the formula and name of the compound.

items: The total positive charge equals the total negative charge.
Use brackets for a group of atoms when more than one is needed.

blocks.text: The name comes from the two ions. The metal (or ammonium) comes first. The ending of the second part tells you what it contains.

items: **-ide** is used when the negative ion is a single element: chloride, oxide, sulfide. Hydroxide also ends in -ide.
**-ate** is used when the negative ion contains oxygen as well: sulfate, nitrate, carbonate, phosphate.
Sodium chloride is NaCl. Sodium sulfate is Na₂SO₄.
-ide means one element (or hydroxide). -ate means the ion also contains oxygen.

checks.q: Describe the structure of an ionic compound such as sodium chloride.
checks.a: A giant lattice (regular arrangement) of positive and negative ions, held together by strong electrostatic forces of attraction between oppositely charged ions that act in all directions.

checks.q: Write the formula of aluminium oxide. The ions are Al³⁺ and O²⁻.
The solid contains only NH₄⁺ and NO₃⁻ ions. Give its formula and name.

exam_phrases: (which) act in all directions (in the giant structure)
(so) need a lot of energy to break the many strong bonds

mistakes.wrong: Aluminium oxide has a high melting point because it has strong ionic bonds.
mistakes.right: 'Strong ionic bonds' is ignored for the first mark. Say strong electrostatic forces of attraction between oppositely charged ions.

mistakes.wrong: A lot of energy is needed to break the bond between one pair of ions.
mistakes.right: The forces act in all directions in the giant structure. Many strong bonds must be broken, so a lot of energy is needed.

worked_example.question:
Aluminium is extracted by the electrolysis of a molten mixture. The mixture contains aluminium oxide and one other substance. Aluminium oxide is an ionic compound.

Explain why aluminium oxide has a very high melting point.
answer_points: Between oppositely charged ions (Al³⁺ and O²⁻).
Which act in all directions in the giant structure.
So a lot of energy is needed to break the many strong bonds.
worked_example.tip: One mark each. Name the forces, say between what, say they act in all directions, then link to energy.

exam_phrases: lattice of positive and negative ions
strong electrostatic forces of attraction / ionic bonds

mistakes.wrong: The solid is called ammonia nitrate.
mistakes.right: Ammonia nitrate is rejected. The ion is ammonium, so the name is ammonium nitrate.

mistakes.wrong: The barium ion in BaCl₂ is Ba₂.
mistakes.right: A subscript is rejected for the charge. Write Ba²⁺ (or Ba+2).

mistakes.wrong: The formula of sodium chloride is Na⁺ + Cl⁻.
mistakes.right: Na⁺ + Cl⁻ is rejected as a final answer. Write the formula NaCl.

worked_example.question:
The solid used in an experiment contained only NH₄⁺ ions and NO₃⁻ ions.

Give the formula and the name of the solid.
worked_example.tip: Use capital letters and write the 4 and the 3 as subscripts.

mistakes.right: Pb²⁺ needs two Br⁻ to balance the charge, so the formula is PbBr₂.

mistakes.wrong: The aluminium ion in AlCl₃ is Al⁺.
mistakes.right: Three Cl⁻ ions need three positive charges to balance them, so the ion is Al³⁺.

worked_example.question:
Electrolysis can be used to separate the elements in some compounds using electricity.

Molten lead bromide contains lead ions, Pb2+, and bromide ions, Br−.

What is the formula for lead bromide?

Tick (✓) one box.

PbBr
PbBr2
Pb2Br
Pb2Br2
worked_example.tip: Balance the charges: one Pb²⁺ needs two Br⁻.
